summary: The script is already within the two-minute limit at roughly 105 words. The main gains are replacing idioms like "holding up", "nudge" and "on track" with literal wording, and swapping a few l- and r-heavy words for easier alternatives.

suggestions.original: Last week we finished the database migration
suggestions.replacement: Last week we completed the database migration
suggestions.reason: Formal, precise verb suits a technical update; easy to say.
Numeral is quicker to read at a fast pace; wording still sounds natural.
Plainer, more literal wording; avoids the l sound in "flaky".
Hyphenated compound reads as one clear term when spoken.
Softer, literal phrasing for bad news; avoids the l in "flag".

suggestions.original: that review is holding up the authentication work
suggestions.replacement: that review is delaying the authentication work
suggestions.reason: Literal wording for international listeners; softens the news.

suggestions.original: If someone can nudge the security team
suggestions.replacement: If someone can follow up with the security team
suggestions.reason: Replaces the colloquial "nudge" with a literal request.

suggestions.original: stay on track for the release
suggestions.replacement: stay on schedule for the release
suggestions.reason: Literal phrase that international listeners will parse easily.
Removes a filler word; the handoff stays clear.
